finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> has no object-level authorization: any caller can retrieve any customer's full invoice record by ID, while the sibling /my/invoice/<inv_id> enforces an ownership check.
finding.source: inv_id path parameter (line 8), supplied by any HTTP client.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at line 10 returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and any other fields.

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup; only the None check (abort 404) guards it.
Full record returned with no comparison to g.user.

finding.guards_checked: No decorator, no g.user reference, no role or admin check in the file. Compared against /my/invoice/<inv_id> (lines 16-17), which checks inv['customer'] != g.user['id'] and that check is absent here. Unverified: whether the app applies a global before_request auth hook outside this repo; even if it does, nothing here restricts by owner. Possible intent as an admin endpoint is not evidenced by any admin check.

verdict.guard_found: none in invoices.py. The only check is the None/404 guard at invoices.py:9 (`INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404)`), which tests existence, not ownership. No auth decorator on the route (invoices.py:7), and no g.user comparison before jsonify at invoices.py:10. The sibling route enforces `inv["customer"] != g.user["id"]` at invoices.py:16-17, which is absent here. The repo has no before_request hook or definition of g.user (the Grep found g.user only at lines 16 and 23), so any global auth lives outside this repo and could at most require a login. It would not restrict access to the invoice owner.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches invoices.py:7-10, and the only guard, the existence check at invoices.py:9, does not compare the record's customer to the caller, unlike the owner check at invoices.py:16-17 on the sibling route. Any caller who gets past an external login gate can read any invoice ID, and the finding's "any caller" wording depends on that unverified external gate.
